status: DRAFT flag kept until the whole palace is modelled. The stated values come from CONTROL-DIMENSIONS.md and are final. The tolerance policy and the part naming below are DECIDED (Bear, 2026-10-17); what is left open is listed in decisions_needed. Run against real models since 2026-10-17: slice 01 (17 of 17), the first six bays (19 of 19) and the first twelve bays (25 gated pass, 4 text controls reported); the controls for the transept, trusses, vault and north strip have no parts to test yet.

decided.decision: D19a is the truss face to face, stated 71.2 ft, tolerance 0.4 ft, plate-checked (the 72 ft centre to centre is D08); D19b stays plate-printed at 6.0 ft, tolerance 0.1 ft.

part_id is the unique ID and part_kind the kind; column_shaft is split from column_base; single-part controls select a 'sample' property, not a name; plan rows are whole-word 'tags' read with the tag selector; require_props makes an untagged part an error; the origin is the centre of the nave and transept crossing.

model_conventions.units: metres, scene unit scale 1.0 (BLENDER.md); this file states feet, the script converts
model_conventions.axes: X = length of the building (east-west, +X east), Y = width (south to north, +Y north; the 48 ft strip is on +Y), Z = up
model_conventions.origin: the centre of the nave and transept crossing, at floor level. The controls use only differences, so the origin does not affect them. Plate I puts the crossing about mid-length (924 ft from either end); confirm that when modelling. The north strip runs from 216 ft to 1152 ft from the west end (Plate I's chain 216 + 936 + 696)
model_conventions.floor: the ground floor slab's top face is at z = 0
model_conventions.parts: A part is a mesh object, or an empty that instances a collection (ARCHITECTURE.md section 6). Each part carries the custom properties below. The collections that are only instance sources must be unlinked from the scene, or they would be measured as parts at their own location
model_conventions.column_shaft: the column above the floor: B's top 3 3/4 in above the floor plus A (18 ft 8 in), so its top is 18 ft 11 3/4 in above the floor and it is 8 in across. Its origin and bounding box are centred on the column axis, so the centre of the part is the column centreline. Everything that is not symmetric about the axis (the flare and base plate, below the floor) is a separate column_base part
model_conventions.tier: tier = the tier a girder, connecting piece or ridge serves (a connecting piece carries the girders of its tier); top_tier = the highest tier a column reaches. Gallery floors use level instead (1 = the gallery at 22 ft 11 in)

custom properties on every placed part.part_id: unique ID, the same as the object name (BLENDER.md section 4)
custom properties on every placed part.part_kind: column_shaft | column_upper | column_base | connecting_piece | girder | truss | gallery_floor | balustrade | floor_ground | ridge | vault_rib | stair_flight | stair_landing | stair_column
custom properties on every placed part.level: 1 (gallery floors and balustrades: the gallery at 22 ft 11 in)
custom properties on every placed part.block: main | north (columns only; north = the 936 x 48 ft strip; the strip's inner row of columns belongs to main)
custom properties on every placed part.tags: space-separated whole words: nave_edge (the two column rows bounding the 72 ft nave), avenue_A1 (the two rows bounding one 48 ft avenue), north_strip_edge (the two rows bounding the strip's 48 ft depth, along its 936 ft); west_end (the columns on the west end line), avenue_void_end (the columns on the line where the avenue voids begin, 24 ft in), nave_void_end (the line where the nave void begins, 72 ft in), stair_gap_west and stair_gap_east (the two lines either side of a 24 ft stair bay, 192 and 216 ft in). A part may carry several
custom properties on every placed part.span_ft: 24 | 48 | 72 (girders and trusses: the bay they carry)
custom properties on every placed part.sample: marks the one part a single-part control measures: shaft_a (D13), girder_24_x (D10b), stair_landing (D27, D28, D31), stair_column (D30), stair_flight (D32), cross_gallery (D33, D34)
custom properties on every placed part.stage: lower | upper (stair flights: from the floor to the landing, or from the landing to the gallery)
custom properties on every placed part.avenue: N | S (stair parts: which avenue void the staircase is in)

object names.column_upper: COLU_T{tier}_X{i:02d}_Y{j:02d} (the 16 ft 7 1/2 in column standing on the connecting piece of the tier below; added when slice 01 was built)
object names.girder: GIRX_T{tier}_X{i:02d}_Y{j:02d} (runs along X) or GIRY_T{tier}_X{i:02d}_Y{j:02d} (along Y); the grid cell is the girder's midpoint
object names.gallery_floor: GFLR_L1_X{i:02d}_Y{j:02d} (one 24 x 24 ft panel per cell, j the lower row)
object names.balustrade: BAL_L1_X{i:02d}_Y{j:02d} (one 24 ft run along a void edge; added when the gallery was built)
object names.stair parts (added with the first stairc: XGAL_{N|S}_X{bay} cross gallery (part_kind gallery_floor, level 1); STLD_{N|S}_X{bay} landing; STCL_{N|S}_X{bay}_{ix}{iy} landing column; STFL_{N|S}_X{bay}_{W|E} ground flight; STFU_{N|S}_X{bay}_{IN|OUT} upper flight; STRL_{N|S}_X{bay}_{E|F}{k} landing railing (part_kind balustrade, level landing); BALY_L1_X{line}_Y{j} cross railing at a void end

naming.instance sources (collections, not linke: PART_ColumnShaft, PART_ColumnUpper, PART_ColumnBase, PART_ConnectingPiece, PART_Girder24, PART_GalleryPanel, PART_Balustrade24, PART_Truss72, PART_Ridge, PART_Rib, PART_Balustrade8, PART_StairFlight, PART_StairLanding, PART_StairColumn, PART_CrossGallery
naming.rules: Names use letters, digits and underscores only, under 63 characters, with zero-padded indices so no .001 suffix appears (BLENDER.md section 5). Controls never select by name: a rename must not break a control. Group the parts by kind in collections for the Outliner; the selectors do not use collections. ARCHITECTURE.md section 6 also asks for unit, erection_order, source_sheet and ledger_row on every part; this file does not need them

tolerance_policy: DECIDED by Bear, 2026-10-17. plate-printed controls: the plate prints the figure and the model is built to it, so the tolerance is a tight modelling tolerance (a few hundredths of a foot). plate-checked controls: the figure is a reading off a plate, so the tolerance is the larger of 0.5% and the sheet's scale-bar scatter (0.7% on Plates VI and XVIII), as ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 item 2 says. Exceptions, each stated in its own tolerance_basis: D19b (plate-printed, but 0.1 ft, because the plate drawing resolves no better) and D18 (plate-checked, but its printed pieces sum exactly, so the 0.5% floor is looser than the evidence; reclassify D18 as plate-printed if a tight gate is wanted).

not_included.why: base plates come in four sizes (2 x 1, 2 x 1.5, 3 x 1.5, 3 x 2 ft) on column_base parts, but the table does not say which columns take which, or which side is the length. Add per-variant controls with sample properties once the variants are modelled.
concrete depth is a range (1 to 4 ft varying with load), and this script compares to a single value.
consistent with D20 but not an independent measurement.
the 108 ft louvre run is on no plate; the text figure is not a control.

controls.what: 72 ft truss across the nave, face to face (the 72 ft is centre to centre of columns, tested as D08)
controls.tolerance_basis: 0.4 ft is 0.56%, above the 0.5% floor. 71.2 is the midpoint of four independent estimates, 70.8 to 71.6 ft, and is NOT a printed figure: Plate XX scaled by its 8 ft panels gives 70.84-71.06; Plate XX scaled by its own printed 36 ft gives 71.18-71.60; 72 ft less an 8 in column across gives 71.33; 72 ft less the cast girders' 4 3/8 in end gap (Plate X prints 23 ft 3 1/4 in face to face for 24 ft) gives 71.27. Tolerance decided by Bear, 2026-10-17

controls.what: 72 ft truss depth (6 ft)
controls.tolerance_basis: the printed 6 ft runs from the top of the top rail to the underside of the bottom rail, so it is outer to outer: the arrow tips read 5.93 ft and the rail bands 6.10 ft; the truss part must have no protruding plates or rivet heads. 0.1 ft is about what the plate drawing resolves, so this is an exception to 'a few hundredths of a foot'. Decided by Bear, 2026-10-17
